key_insight: Parallel use of multiple on-premises QPUs can accelerate fragment-based quantum chemistry without sacrificing chemical accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that distributed quantum workflows can raise sampling throughput on prototype hardware, informing how future HPC centers may integrate many QPUs as shared resources.
method: Used fragment molecular orbital (FMO) decomposition for helium cluster energy calculations.
Compared synchronous shot-parallel QWFS sampling with asynchronous fragment-parallel execution across three Quoll QPUs.
Applied SPAM correction and device-specific circuit optimization to assemble final FMO-QWFS energies.
evidence_signal: The three-QPU shot-parallel workflow achieved 93.60% parallel efficiency, while fragment-parallel execution reached 75.01% measured efficiency and 95.17% excluding idle job time, with chemically accurate energies in both modes.
watch_item: Reported efficiency depends on job scheduling and non-interruptible idle time, so real-world gains may be lower if queueing and device availability are constrained.
paper_title: Demonstration of Parallel Multi-QPU Execution for Fragment-Based Quantum Chemistry Using On-Premises Hardware
